channel.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
channel.description: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

item.title: How stores choose what to put on their shelves — like, say, Planet Money's board game
item.description: The most coveted real estate in business might just be the choicest shelf space of national big box retail. We go inside the room and the process of how stores choose what you can and can't buy.
item.content:encoded: The most coveted real estate in business might just be the choicest shelf space of national big box retail. We go inside the room and the process of how stores choose what you can and can't buy.
item.dc:creator: Kenny Malone

item.title: Foreign ministers of the Americas to discuss Nicaragua in meeting called by the U.S.
item.description: The U.S. is pushing the Americas to confront Nicaragua—but what, if anything, the region is prepared to do remains unclear.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. is pushing the Americas to confront Nicaragua—but what, if anything, the region is prepared to do remains unclear.

item.title: Demand for ambulance helicopters is going up, but it's hard to retain staff
item.description: Rural hospital closures are driving demand for air ambulance services. But finding and keeping highly trained staff to practice medicine in the air isn't easy.
item.content:encoded: Rural hospital closures are driving demand for air ambulance services. But finding and keeping highly trained staff to practice medicine in the air isn't easy.
item.dc:creator: Elaine Appleton-Grant

item.title: Here's what's on the docket for Pope Leo XIV's first papal visit to France since 2008
item.description: In the first papal state visit to France in nearly 20 years, Pope Leo will preside over Mass in Paris, meet with sex abuse survivors and deliver a speech on European unity.
item.content:encoded: In the first papal state visit to France in nearly 20 years, Pope Leo will preside over Mass in Paris, meet with sex abuse survivors and deliver a speech on European unity.

item.title: Thousands of people gather for a South African barbecue, aiming to set a world record
item.description: South Africa is aiming to smash a savory world record — the world's largest BBQ — and more boerewors sausage than you can shake a stick at.

item.title: Media reporter Oliver Darcy unpacks the story behind President Trump's press ban
item.description: Part of the Trump administration's argument for banning news outlets is that their coverage posed a threat to national security. A story cited an anonymous official, who turned out to be VP Vance.

item.title: President Trump's FDA commissioner nom, Dr. Heidi Overton, faces Senators' questions
item.description: Dr. Heidi Overton has been nominated to be the new FDA commissioner. The Senate HELP committee pressed her on vaccines, mifepristone, food safety and whether she can tell the president he's wrong.

item.title: Increasingly isolated Netanyahu makes defiant speech at UN
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave an address to the United Nations General Assembly amid wide criticism of Israel's conduct in Gaza. Meanwhile, Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas delivered an address via pre-recorded video.

item.title: A Catholic media star was beatified in St. Louis, moving a step closer to sainthood
item.description: Bishop Fulton Sheen will be beatified by the Catholic Church in St. Louis on Thursday, moving the television personality from the 1950s one step away from sainthood.

item.title: Past presidents have invoked national security, but Trump takes it to new level
item.description: President Trump invokes "national security" to defend actions like banning reporters and building a new ballroom and arch. Critics note judges are often deferential to presidents making this claim.
